questions.question: A wave is travelling along a string . At an instant the shape of the string is as shown in figure. At this instant, point A is moving upward, then select the correct option.
options: Wave is travelling to the left
Amplitude of all the particles are same.
At this instant, velocity of C is directed downward.
questions.explanation:
Question Explanation: Analyzing particle motion in a wave.

Concept: Transverse Wave Properties.

Solution:

\tDirection of Wave: We are given that point A is moving upward. For this to happen, the wave shape must be moving to the left. If it were moving right, point A would be moving downward. So, statement (1) is correct.
\tAmplitude: In a simple harmonic wave, every particle of the medium oscillates with the same amplitude (maximum displacement). So, statement (2) is correct.
\tVelocity of C: Since the wave is travelling to the left, we can determine the motion of point C. The part of the wave to the right of C is lower. As the wave moves left, point C must move downward to match the approaching shape. So, statement (3) is correct.

Since all three statements are correct, the final answer is "All the above".

Final Answer:(4)

questions.question: 2 moles of an ideal gas expands reversibly and adiabatically so its temperature changes from 300 K to 290 K. Calculate work done (Cp = 8 cal/mol-K)
questions.explanation:
1. Question explanation 
We are asked to calculate the work done when 2 moles of an ideal gas expand reversibly and adiabatically, causing its temperature to drop from 300 K to 290 K. We are given Cp = 8cal / mol.K. 
2. Concept 
For a reversible adiabatic process, the work done is related to the change in internal energy: 
W = ΔE = nCvΔT 
where: 
• Cv = Cp – R 
• ΔT = T2 – T1 (final - initial) 
We will first find Cv, then compute W. 
3. Calculation (if any)
Given: 
• Cp = 8cal / mol.K
• R = 2cal / mol.K
• Cv = Cp – R = 8 – 2 = 6cal / mol.K
Calculate ΔT : 
ΔT = 290K - 300K = – 10K 
Calculate work done: 
W = nCvΔT = 2 × 6 cal/mol . K × (–10 K) –120 cal 
4. Final answer : 
Option 1. –120cal

Reabsorption of Na+ along with excretion of K+ is controlled by which one of the following hormones?
questions.explanation:
Solution/Explanation: 
The hormone that controls the reabsorption of Na+ along with the excretion of K+ is Aldosterone. 
Here’s why: 
Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex. 
Its primary function is to regulate blood pressure and electrolyte balance. 
It acts on the kidneys to increase the reabsorption of sodium (Na+) ions from the urine back into the bloodstream. 
At the same time, it promotes the excretion of potassium (K+) ions in the urine.This mechanism helps maintain the body's fluid and electrolyte balance, as well as blood pressure. 

Conclusion: 
Hence, option (2) is correct.

questions.explanation:
Question Explaination:

The user wants to identify the primary physiological effect of the hormone glucagon.

Concept:

Endocrine System; Blood Glucose Regulation.

Solution:

Glucagon is a hormone released by the pancreas when blood sugar levels are low. It signals the liver to break down stored glycogen (glycogenolysis) and release glucose into the bloodstream. This action raises the blood glucose concentration, so it is classified as a hyperglycemic hormone. It has the opposite effect of insulin.

Final Answer:

Hyperglycemic hormone
